page: Amazon Web Services c8id.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance hosted on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz, providing 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR5 system memory running at 7 GHz, presenting a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration instructions include Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX tile and INT8) to support targeted mathematical and cryptographic compute routines.

For I/O operations, the instance incorporates 237 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD instance storage. This ephemeral disk provides low-latency access for temporary files, caching layers, and intermediate build artifacts. Network connectivity provides a baseline throughput of 2 Gbps. The instance does not feature dedicated GPU acceleration, relying entirely on the Intel Xeon CPU for processing tasks.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded throughput, led by a Geekbench single-core score of 2202.0, single-threaded gzip compression speeds of 34.39 GB/sec, and high text-processing throughput. In contrast, multi-threaded scaling reflects its 4-vCPU capacity, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 5013.0 and moderate passmark multi-core figures. The DDR5 memory subsystem delivers stable uncached read and write bandwidth, although cached memory performance registers lower in benchmark comparisons.

The qualitative hardware balance makes the c8id.xlarge an efficient platform for compute-oriented workloads requiring fast single-thread execution alongside local storage scratch space. Best-fit use cases include software compilation via Clang, single-threaded compression and ETL pipelines, static web serving, and lightweight key-value caching operations such as Redis.
description: Amazon Web Services c8id.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by a 3.9 GHz Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor within the Nitro hypervisor framework. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores, 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 7 GHz, and a built-in 237 GB NVMe SSD for fast local ephemeral storage. Hardware capabilities include AVX-512 and AMX extensions for matrix-vector mathematics, paired with a 2 Gbps baseline network throughput. Benchmark evaluations highlight exceptional single-threaded efficiency, scoring 2202.0 in Geekbench single-core tests and delivering 34.39 GB/sec in gzip compression, alongside solid text processing capabilities. Conversely, multi-core throughput and memory access latency reflect the constraints of its 4-vCPU scale. With dedicated processing cores and attached NVMe disk performance, c8id.xlarge serves workloads such as software compilation, static web serving, localized cache operations, and batch data transformation routines.
